title: ClickHouse cert-rotate: Vault Agent re-render + SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG
description: The nexus-cli cert-rotate verb for ClickHouse: force a fresh mTLS leaf from the clickhouse-server PKI role (Vault Agent re-render), split it into server.crt/server.key/ca.crt, and have ClickHouse pick it up via SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG (no full restart). Verifies the cert serial changes + TLS still validates.

observe.what: the current leaf serial -- record as $SERIAL_BEFORE

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 'sudo rm -f /etc/clickhouse-server/tls/bundle.pem; sudo systemctl restart nexus-vault-agent.service; sleep 6; sudo /usr/local/sbin/clickhouse-tls-split.sh /etc/clickhouse-server/tls clickhouse'

observe.what: Vault Agent re-issues a fresh leaf from pki_int/issue/clickhouse-server; the split script writes new server.crt/key/ca.crt

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --accept-invalid-certificate --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG'; sudo openssl x509 -in /etc/clickhouse-server/tls/server.crt -noout -serial"

observe.what: a NEW serial (!= $SERIAL_BEFORE) -- the rotated leaf is live; SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG re-reads the openSSL cert files without a restart
TLS still validates with the rotated cert (returns 1) -- no downtime

whatProves: cert-rotate forces a fresh Vault-PKI leaf, re-renders the on-node TLS material, and ClickHouse picks it up via SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG with no restart + no TLS downtime -- the 90-day rotation path the ClickHouseAdapter cert-rotate verb triggers.
